newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico shrs rally in late trade on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Mexico shrs rally in late trade on foreign buying.

text.p: Mexican stocks sharply extended early gains in brisk late trade on Wednesday, as foreign investors rushed to buy blue chips on cue from gains notched up on Wall Street, traders said.
The leading IPC share index was up 60.15 points, or 1.58 percent, at 3,865.25.
"It's a combination of foreigners stepping in and a rebound in several blue chips that had been in the doldrums for a few days," a floor trader said.
Trading volume was heavy and much improved on many recent sessions at 128.4 million shares.

Traders drew attention to gains by bellwether Telmex L shares, which were up 58 centavos to an intraday record of 16.86 pesos, while its ADRs climbed 1-5/8 to 42-3/4, a level not seen since the December 1994 peso devaluation crisis.
"Telmex is going great guns. I think they're buying ahead of expected good earnings for the first quarter," a trader said.
